adversarial_review.check: Conjugation is on the first vector in every Gram sum and the product difference uses conjugate(f-g) f plus conjugate(g)(f-g).
Hamiltonian, oscillator dimension, graph edges, parameters, sources, beta values and tau values are read from the manifest or canonical Q3 builder; no physical number is inserted from the output.
The raw inequality is evaluated before division by the positive partition function, and the script separately checks positivity of every declared finite partition.

Independent diagonalization may choose a different basis in a degenerate subspace; the integrated comparison records this with an explicit manifest tolerance and does not call coordinate equality a carrier identification.
All source sites of the three finite graphs are recomputed, but finite coverage is not a source-uniform thermodynamic estimate.
Every decomposition and bound row has finite fields, an explicit absolute-plus-relative tolerance, and a nonnegative recorded slack within that tolerance.
The independent lane rebuilds oscillator tensors, Q3 Hamiltonians, spectra, characters, transfer matrices and complex sums without importing the primary lane.
The finite Complex bridge does not close a cross-volume common OS carrier, exhaustion Cauchy, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite Complex Q3 transfer-word instantiation. It is not a common OS Hilbert-carrier theorem, a thermodynamic limit, a common-alpha construction, a mass-gap proof, a continuum result, or a Clay result.
decision_reason: The finite Q3 OS transfer-word matrices now instantiate the Complex Hilbert-Schmidt bridge rather than a Real-only toy fixture. This closes a precise finite interface for subsequent analytic estimates, but it does not supply an isometric transport between different volumes or any source, volume, cutoff or beta uniformity.
finding: R340 proves the exact Complex inequality |G_f(i,j)-G_g(i,j)| <= sum_k |f(i,k)-g(i,k)| |f(j,k)| + sum_k |g(i,k)| |f(j,k)-g(j,k)|. The primary lane passes 234/234 assertions and 96 rows, the independent lane passes 235/235 and 96 rows, and the integrated lane passes 11/11 with Lean PASS. The two lanes agree within the declared 1e-4 comparison tolerance; the largest raw discrepancy is caused by independent eigenspace bases on a finite degenerate spectrum, not by a failed R340 inequality. The minimum normalized slack is approximately 0.0012248084683 and the largest normalized decomposition residual is below 4e-14 in both lanes.
method: Compile verification/lean/Tect/R340.lean with the pinned Lean toolchain and require a zero exit status with no Lean errors.
Build the declared d=3 Q3 Hamiltonian independently on bond2, square4 and grid2x3, diagonalize each finite Hamiltonian, and form the energy-basis transfer-word matrices at every declared source site.

For each graph, source, beta and the two declared tau contexts, flatten the q and p transfer-word matrices into complex Hilbert-Schmidt vectors and compute all four Gram-entry differences and the two R340 right-hand terms.
Require the conjugate-product decomposition residual and the R340 bound within the manifest absolute and relative tolerances, then repeat the calculation in a non-importing independent lane.
Run the integrated verifier to compare row keys and numerical fields within the declared eigenspace-basis tolerance, rerun Lean R340 and enforce the finite-only QFT scope firewall.
next_action: Use the recorded vector-difference terms as the input contract for a cross-volume common-carrier test. Prove an explicit isometric transport or a source/volume/cutoff/beta-uniform bound; if neither can be derived for the exact Q3 data, register that missing-interface obstruction rather than promoting finite Gram control.
no_overclaim: This record promotes only the finite Complex R340 theorem and its numerical instantiation on the declared Q3 matrices. It does not prove a common OS Hilbert space, thermodynamic dynamics, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, a GNS mass gap, continuum removal, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.
